query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Incorporating a modest volume fraction (around 5–10%) of a ductile, low-melting metal that is fully miscible with the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 matrix (for example, tin) during alloy synthesis can promote an in‐situ formation of a fine, interconnected second phase. This second phase will preferentially locate at grain boundaries and within the matrix to blunt crack propagation while not interfering with the intrinsic caloric phase transformation, thus simultaneously improving mechanical integrity and preserving the high caloric response.
generation.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy that displays a single‐phase but relatively brittle microstructure, yielding a large caloric effect yet prone to cracking under mechanical load.
generation.intervention: Introduce approximately 5–10 vol% of a selected ductile, low-melting metal (e.g., tin) during processing to induce in-situ precipitation of a fine, ductile second phase.
generation.conditions: Under operational conditions typical for caloric measurements, i.e., applied magnetic and pressure fields at the alloy’s transformation temperature, as well as under compressive load (analogous to the regimes used in prior strength tests).
generation.structural_mediator: A refined, interconnected ductile second phase distributed along grain boundaries and within the bulk microstructure.
generation.mechanism: The added low-melting metal forms a secondary phase during controlled cooling or heat treatment. This phase, while minor in volume, provides crack deflection/arrest capabilities and improves overall energy absorption during mechanical loading, thereby increasing compressive strength without disrupting the phase transformation that underpins the caloric effect.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in compressive strengths toward or above the 150 MPa range (comparable to or exceeding epoxy-containing composites) with minimal reduction in the large caloric response. The improved toughness should mitigate localized stress concentrations under applied fields and loads.
generation.baseline: The unchanged (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy exhibits high caloric performance but poor mechanical integrity (with compressive strengths significantly lower and an obvious propensity to crack).
generation.boundary: Within the operational ranges of applied-field and pressure-field caloric measurement and under compressive loading conditions typical for the material’s use. The chosen ductile metal must remain rare-earth-free and not form deleterious phases under these processing and loading conditions.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal volume fraction and the exact identity of the ductile metal require further experimental tuning. There is also uncertainty regarding the extent to which interphase boundaries might affect the microscopic caloric transformation kinetics.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of samples of the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy with 0%, 5%, and 10% addition of a ductile metal such as tin. Apply identical thermal processing and heat treatments to promote in-situ phase formation. Characterize the microstructure (using SEM/TEM) to verify the formation and distribution of the second phase. Then perform compressive mechanical testing and caloric effect measurements under the same applied magnetic and pressure fields.
measurements: Microstructure (grain size and secondary phase distribution)
Caloric response metrics (e.g., entropy change, temperature change) under field application
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the samples containing the ductile secondary phase do not demonstrate a statistically significant increase in mechanical integrity (e.g., compressive strength remains similar to or lower than the baseline) or if the caloric response is substantially degraded compared to the unmodified alloy, then the hypothesis is falsified.
